about: Spilled arrays (ADR-0125): the layout of a spill, its obstacles, what reads it, how it moves with the Sheet's structure, and the recalculation passes a layout costs (ADR-0124). Transcribed from SpillTests.cs.

cases.name: ADR-0125: a Reference to several cells spills from its Anchor, and the cells it covers hold no Entry
ADR-0125: a spill is not recorded in a Sheet Document, and reopening lays it out again
ADR-0125: a blank in the array shows as 0, as Excel's spill of a blank cell does
ADR-0125: an Entry in the way is #SPILL!, nothing is overwritten, and clearing it lets the Formula spill
ADR-0125: typing into a spilled cell enters an Entry there, and the Anchor becomes #SPILL!
ADR-0125: a spill past the Sheet's edge is #SPILL!
ADR-0125: of two spills that would overlap, the Anchor first in address order spills, whichever was entered first: D1 then C2
cases.note: D1 spills D1:D3 down; C2 would spill C2:D2 across, and D2 is D1's. D1 comes first.

cases.name: ADR-0125: of two spills that would overlap, the Anchor first in address order spills, whichever was entered first: C2 then D1
cases.note: D1 spills D1:D3 down; C2 would spill C2:D2 across, and D2 is D1's. D1 comes first.

cases.name: ADR-0125: a Formula that reads a spilled cell is recalculated when the spill changes
ADR-0125: a spill that shrinks releases the cells it no longer covers
ADR-0125: clearing the Anchor clears its spill
ADR-0125: a function that reduces an array takes it whole
ADR-0125: a spill moves with its Anchor when rows are inserted above it
ADR-0125: a row inserted inside the spill grows the range it reads, and the spill with it
ADR-0125 / ADR-0049: a Linked Table's column spills, and follows its rows
ADR-0125: #SPILL! propagates as any Error Value does
ADR-0125: A1# reads the Spill Range of the Formula in A1, and follows it as it grows
ADR-0125: A1# spills itself, as a Reference to several cells does
ADR-0125: A1# is #REF! when A1 does not spill: no Formula, one Value, or #SPILL!
ADR-0125: A1# is written as typed, moves with A1, and is #REF! when A1 is deleted
ADR-0125: # follows one cell only, and the @ operator is refused on entry: =A1:A2#
ADR-0125: # follows one cell only, and the @ operator is refused on entry: =A:A#
ADR-0125: # follows one cell only, and the @ operator is refused on entry: =@A1:A2
ADR-0125: # follows one cell only, and the @ operator is refused on entry: =SUM(@A1:A2)
ADR-0125: an array larger than the engine holds is refused with #NUM!, never cut short: =SUM(1001:2025*1)
ADR-0125: an array larger than the engine holds is refused with #NUM!, never cut short: =SUM(A:Q*1)
ADR-0125: an array larger than the engine holds is refused with #NUM!, never cut short: =SEQUENCE(1048576,17)
ADR-0125: an array larger than the engine holds is refused with #NUM!, never cut short: =SUM(A1:A1048576+B1:XFD1)
ADR-0125: part of a spill copied without its Anchor pastes as Values, as Excel's does
ADR-0125: a spill copied with its Anchor pastes the Formula, which spills again
ADR-0125, ADR-0124: a Reference OFFSET computes into a Spill Range reads it as the layout leaves it, blocked or freed, as a typed one does
ADR-0125, ADR-0124, ADR-0180: a volatile Formula read again after a layout draws as it drew before the layout: the obstacle in A2
cases.note: B1 draws the same whether A1's spill is blocked or not.

cases.name: ADR-0125, ADR-0124, ADR-0180: a volatile Formula read again after a layout draws as it drew before the layout: the obstacle in A5
cases.note: B1 draws the same whether A1's spill is blocked or not.

cases.name: ADR-0124, ADR-0125: a blocked Anchor whose INDIRECT is read again after the layout stays #SPILL!, and spills when freed
ADR-0124, ADR-0125: a blocked OFFSET Anchor stays #SPILL! through a change elsewhere
ADR-0180, ADR-0125: a blocked Anchor that draws stays #SPILL!, whether it is entered or recalculated after
ADR-0124, ADR-0125: every volatile Formula is computed once, and once more after each layout that changes something

steps.note: A3 blocks A1's spill (one layout), which shrinks C1's (a second): three passes, and the INDIRECT reads the second layout, which no Dependent would have told it of.
